conversation.content:
Hello there—thank you for taking a few minutes with me. I’m Dr. Ramirez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. My job is simply to listen and help you feel supported as you adjust to life with your new baby.

Today we’ll use the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale, or EPDS. It’s a brief, 10-question screen that looks at how you’ve been feeling emotionally over the past seven days. Many new parents find it helpful because it puts words to the ups and downs that can come after birth. There are no right or wrong answers, and everything you share stays between us unless there’s an immediate safety concern.

I’ll read each question conversationally, and you can just tell me what feels closest to your experience. Ready to begin?

In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Yeah, I can still laugh. Maybe not quite as easily as before the baby—like, sometimes I’ll hear a joke and smile but not feel that full-on laugh I used to. It’s not every day, but yes, I can still find things funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Most days I can still laugh, just maybe not quite as heartily as before—like, I’ll chuckle at something on my phone or my partner’s silly faces with the baby, but it feels a little muted, not the big belly laughs I used to have.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to stuff—coffee with my best friend tomorrow, maybe a short walk later—but the excitement is kind of mild, not the big “can’t-wait” feeling I used to get. It’s more like, “That’ll be nice,” rather than really buzzing about it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Not really. If the baby spits up a ton or won’t settle, I might think “maybe I ate something that bothers him” or “did I miss a burp?”—but it’s fleeting. I don’t stay stuck on it or beat myself up; I figure babies are just unpredictable.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll suddenly feel a little on-edge—like, the baby’s asleep and nothing’s actually wrong, but my chest gets tight and my mind races through “what-ifs” about his breathing or whether I sterilized the bottles right. It doesn’t last long and it’s not every day, but yeah, it pops up out of nowhere.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky, more like a quick flutter of “uh-oh” that passes in a minute. Like last night I heard him whimper on the monitor and my stomach did a little flip, but once I checked and he was fine, the feeling just melted away.
Things have been getting on top of me
Sometimes, yeah. I’ll be feeding the baby and notice the laundry pile or think about the dishes, and it feels like a lot, but then I remind myself I can only do one thing at a time and it eases off.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, sleeping’s actually been okay—once I finally get to bed I’m out. I’m tired, but it’s more physical tired from the day, not lying there upset or wired.
I have felt sad or miserable
Mostly I feel okay, just a bit flat every now and then—like the color’s turned down a notch. I wouldn’t call it “sad,” more like mellow or neutral, and it never sticks around for the whole day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Hardly at all. I got a little teary on day five when my milk came in and the baby wouldn’t latch, but it was just for a minute, and I haven’t cried since.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. That hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 8: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note (Edinburgh data)

**Symptoms endorsed (mild/subclinical):**  
- Anhedonia (reduced enthusiasm/pleasure, not absent)  
- Episodic, unexplained anxiety/tension with physical component  
- Occasional sense of being overwhelmed; copes with self-talk  
- Flat or “muted” mood, no pervasive sadness or tearfulness  

**Symptoms denied:**  
- Persistent low mood, crying spells, sleep disruption, guilt/worthlessness, self-harm ideation  

**Pattern:**  
Brief, self-limited anxiety spikes and diminished zest, but subjective enjoyment, humor, and daily function largely preserved; no safety concerns elicited  

**Screening significance:**  
Findings below conventional EPDS cut-offs; no indicators suggestive of major depressive or anxiety disorder at present. Continue routine postpartum monitoring, psychoeducation, and re-screen if symptoms worsen or persist.
